text.tspan: Why does it feel like I'm
staying down when I'm not?
Because your head and chest stay
level, so it feels steady. The
movement happens lower down: in your
impact frame your hips are 7% of your
height closer to the ball than at
address. In the wall drill, the moment
your glute leaves the wall is the
moment you would stand up.

g.text: Feel cue, checked against your impact frame

text.tspan: From address to impact your hips moved toward
the ball by 7% of your height. The rule table
flags anything over 4%. When the hips push
forward, your chest has to stand up to make room
for your arms, so the club reaches the ball from
a different height each time. That is where thin
and blocked shots come from. The usual root is
the hips not turning enough: your lead hip had
turned 31° at impact, where we would expect
about 45°. A hip that cannot turn slides toward
the ball instead. That is also why this feels
normal: your head stays level while your hips do
the moving. Start with the wall drill at the
range, and loosen the hips with the 90/90
rotation at home.
Backside against a wall or your golf bag.
Make slow half swings and keep your trail
glute on it through impact.
